To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the periplasmic peptydil-prolyl isomease (PPIase) genes, surA and Fkp A, are important for the starvation-stress resistance of Salmonella.
SurA and FKP are important for the survival of carbon-starved S. typhimurium and that the expression of these two genes during carbon starvation is not σE-dependent.
SurA and FkPA are required for the long-term starvation-stress resistance of Salmonella entericaserovar Typhymurium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and characterizing the σE-dependent genes of Salmonella and determining their contribution to C-starvation resistance and cross-resistance to various environmental stresses.
the identification of the genes involved in starvation-stress response and their role in survival of Salmonella during the stationary phase.

the identification and characterization of genes involved in the starvation-stressed response (SSR), a unique survival strategy that enables Salmonella cells to withstand extended periods of starvation, as well as multiple stressors that would rapidly kill growing cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SSR of Salmonella is a complex process involving a number of different genes and regulatory pathways, and the exact role of SurA and FKP-A in the SSR remains unclear.
SurA and FKP-A are required for long-term C starvation survival and for the resistance of starved cells to heat, low pH and polymyxin B.
surA and Fkp-A are not C-starved inducible, but are important for C-starved survival and cross-resistance to high temperature, low pH, and antimicrobial peptide polymixin B.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SurA and FKP are not starvation-inducible in Salmonella, but are important for the stress resistance of starved Salmonella cells.
SurA and FKP-A are important to Salmonella survival under starvation conditions, but they are not C-starved-inducible.
SurA and FKP A are important in Salmonella for long-term C starvation survival and for the stress resistance of C-starved S. typhimurium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SurA and FkPA are important for C-starved Salmonellae to withstand stress and are part of a larger group of genes that are important for C starved cells to withstand stress.
surA and Fkp-A are important for the SSR of Salmonella, although their roles in the response differ.

surA and, to a lesser extent, fkpA play an essential role in the survival of C-starved Salmonellae, and that the SSR of Salmonella is not simply the sum total of the σE-dependent and -independent responses.
